hook: Visible light and acetaldehyde turn nitrogen in air into nitric acid at 200 C and low pressure.

readout.label: Nitric acid formation rate from air

summary: Acetaldehyde oxidizes to peracetic acid over stainless steel, and light turns that into radicals that oxidize N2 to nitric acid at 1 to 5 bar. The authors report 110.8 umol per hour and 0.45% N2 conversion, far above earlier systems. Yields are lab scale, conversion is low, and energy cost versus current industry is not shown.
title: Acetaldehyde-Mediated Direct Conversion of Air to Nitric Acid
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
